class.name: Geometry2D
class.brief_description: Provides methods for some common 2D geometric operations.
class.description: Provides a set of helper functions to create geometric shapes, compute intersections between shapes, and process various other geometric operations in 2D.

method.name: bresenham_line
method.description: Returns the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bresenham%27s_line_algorithm]Bresenham line[/url] between the [param from] and [param to] points. A Bresenham line is a series of pixels that draws a line and is always 1-pixel thick on every row and column of the drawing (never more, never less). Example code to draw a line between two [Marker2D] nodes using a series of [method CanvasItem.draw_rect] calls: [codeblock] func _draw(): for pixel in Geometry2D.bresenham_line($MarkerA.position, $MarkerB.position): draw_rect(Rect2(pixel, Vector2.ONE), Color.WHITE) [/codeblock]

method.name: clip_polygons
method.description: Clips [param polygon_a] against [param polygon_b] and returns an array of clipped polygons. This performs [constant OPERATION_DIFFERENCE] between polygons. Returns an empty array if [param polygon_b] completely overlaps [param polygon_a]. If [param polygon_b] is enclosed by [param polygon_a], returns an outer polygon (boundary) and inner polygon (hole) which could be distinguished by calling [method is_polygon_clockwise].

method.name: clip_polyline_with_polygon
method.description: Clips [param polyline] against [param polygon] and returns an array of clipped polylines. This performs [constant OPERATION_DIFFERENCE] between the polyline and the polygon. This operation can be thought of as cutting a line with a closed shape.

method.name: convex_hull
method.description: Given an array of [Vector2]s, returns the convex hull as a list of points in counterclockwise order. The last point is the same as the first one.

method.name: decompose_polygon_in_convex
method.description: Decomposes the [param polygon] into multiple convex hulls and returns an array of [PackedVector2Array].

method.name: exclude_polygons
method.description: Mutually excludes common area defined by intersection of [param polygon_a] and [param polygon_b] (see [method intersect_polygons]) and returns an array of excluded polygons. This performs [constant OPERATION_XOR] between polygons. In other words, returns all but common area between polygons. The operation may result in an outer polygon (boundary) and inner polygon (hole) produced which could be distinguished by calling [method is_polygon_clockwise].

method.name: prune_points_min_distance
method.description: Cgame extension: performs deterministic greedy 2D point self-pruning, returning indices of kept points in their original order. Each point is kept only when it is at least [param min_distance] away from [b]every previously kept point[/b]; exactly equal distances are allowed. The first candidate is always retained when [param max_kept] is positive or unlimited. This is an ordered filter, not a stochastic Poisson-disk generator or a reorder/sort operation. [param max_kept] limits the result count; -1 keeps all qualifying points. Ordinary inputs use a 2D spatial hash with a 3×3 neighborhood query. Extreme coordinate-to-radius ratios fall back to an exact full scan rather than overflowing grid coordinates. The entire input is validated before pruning: at most 8192 finite points, finite nonnegative [param min_distance] with a finite squared value, and [param max_kept] between -1 and 8192. Invalid input returns an empty array. A zero minimum distance retains all points, including duplicates, up to the requested maximum. The input array is not modified. Useful for procedural scatter placement, vegetation, props, decals and candidate collision filtering. Does not inspect actual mesh bounds or physics bodies.

method.name: get_nearest_neighbors
method.description: Cgame extension: finds up to [param neighbor_count] nearest other points for [i]each[/i] input point in a single CPU call. Returns one [PackedInt32Array] of [b]input point indices[/b] per input element, ordered by increasing squared Euclidean distance (equal distances break ties by the lowest point index). The point does not match itself, although different indices at the same coordinates are valid neighbors. Candidates at exactly [param max_distance] are included; points with no qualifying neighbors return empty index arrays. All inputs are validated before processing: at most 4096 points, 0–32 neighbors, finite coordinates and a finite nonnegative radius whose square is representable. Invalid input returns an empty outer array. Zero neighbors returns an empty index array for each input. Empty input returns an empty outer array. This performs a bounded [code]O(n² × k)[/code] scan, not a persistent spatial index or a kd-tree; it holds only [code]k[/code] temporary candidates. Best for procedural graph construction from moderate point collections. For repeated queries on many moving points, use a spatial partition or broadphase instead.

method.name: get_closest_point_on_segments
method.description: Returns the nearest point on a collection of independent 2D line segments. [param segment_endpoints] stores pairs of endpoints in order: [code][a0, b0, a1, b1, ...][/code]. A zero-length segment is treated as a point. Returns a [Dictionary] with [code]point[/code] ([Vector2]), [code]distance[/code] ([float]), [code]segment_index[/code] ([int], zero-based), and [code]t[/code] ([float], from 0 at the first endpoint to 1 at the second). Equal-distance results deterministically choose the first matching segment. Returns an empty dictionary for an empty set, an odd number of endpoints, a nonfinite coordinate or more than 32768 segments. Values are checked before any search. This is a linear CPU search; callers handling many queries should partition segments spatially.

method.name: bake_heightfield_curvature_colors
method.description: Cgame extension: bakes terrain cavity (red) and ridge (green) color attributes for a regular heightfield, with blue and alpha set to 1.0. The input [param padded_heights] is row-major with dimensions [code](size.x + 2) * (size.y + 2)[/code]; it must contain exactly one sample of terrain height around each edge of the unpadded output. The four padded corner samples are accepted but never used. For output pixel [code](x, y)[/code], the discrete four-neighbor Laplacian is [code](left + right + up + down - 4 * center) / (cell_spacing * cell_spacing)[/code]. Positive curvature means cavities and negative curvature means ridges. Curvature is converted to two independent [code]smoothstep[/code] ramps using the four optional threshold parameters, all in world-height units per squared world distance. Supplying the true neighboring height samples at chunk boundaries avoids color seams between streamed landscape cells. Output dimensions must be 1–2046 per axis, input heights must be finite and sized correctly, spacing and inverse squared spacing must be positive and representable, and ramp intervals must be finite, increasing and nonnegative. An invalid input yields an empty array. Only CPU colors are returned; upload them separately with [method ChunkedTerrain3D.set_color_data] or another mesh API. This is a reusable curvature attribute baker, not a GPU distance field or screen-space AO effect.

method.name: sample_scalar_grid_wrapped
method.description: Cgame extension: sample a periodic row-major scalar grid at a batch of normalized [param uvs]. Each integer change in U or V repeats the same data, so negative and greater-than-one UVs are supported. The 4 closest lattice values are interpolated bilinearly, wrapping both axes; if [param smooth] is [code]true[/code], each fractional coordinate is first mapped through the cubic [code]t*t*(3-2*t)[/code] smoothstep ease. If [code]false[/code], ordinary bilinear weights are used. The grid represents lattice vertices at normalized integer texel locations, not samples shifted by half a texel. Returns one float per queried coordinate, in the original query order. The input grid and coordinates are not modified. Width and height must each be between 1 and 2048, the grid length must equal width times height, all grid values and UVs must be finite, and at most 65536 UVs can be queried per call. Zero queries return an empty array. Invalid data or non-representable results return an empty array and report an error. This is a CPU batch sampler, not a GPU image texture or a full PCG graph.

method.name: heightfield_gradients
method.description: Cgame extension: computes the two first-order height derivatives for a row-major, regularly spaced heightmap. Returns one [Vector2] per sample: its X component is [code]dheight/dx[/code] and its Y component is [code]dheight/dy[/code]. Each component uses centered differences between adjacent samples, divided by twice [param cell_spacing]. Neighbor coordinates are clamped to the image edge, so outermost samples use the repeated border height and have half the corresponding one-sided slope. Dimensions of 1 are supported, producing zero derivative along that axis. The gradient can be converted to a normalized terrain-facing normal using [code]Vector3(-gradient.x, 1, -gradient.y).normalized()[/code], or used directly for hillshade, slope filtering and procedural landscape masks. This is a CPU-only utility (not a normal-map image encoder or a GPU terrain renderer). [code]size.x[/code] and [code]size.y[/code] must be in the range 1–2048, and [param heights] must contain exactly [code]size.x * size.y[/code] finite values. [param cell_spacing] and its half inverse must be positive, finite and representable. Invalid input or non-representable output gradients returns an empty array. The source heightmap remains unchanged.

method.name: max_filter_mask
method.description: Cgame extension: performs an 8-bit, row-major, square-window maximum filter (grayscale dilation) over a mask. Each output pixel is the maximum source value within [param radius] horizontal and vertical pixels of its location; samples outside the image are ignored. For binary data this grows the occupied area in the eight-connected/Chebyshev metric. For soft masks, the full 0–255 values are preserved by the local maximum rather than thresholding. The implementation uses two separable O(width × height) sliding-window monotone-deque passes with memory proportional to the raster size, independent of [param radius]. Valid image dimensions are between 1 and 2048 inclusive; [param radius] must be in 0–64; and the byte count must equal [code]size.x * size.y[/code]. Invalid arguments return an empty array; zero radius returns the unmodified mask via copy-on-write. This is a CPU image-processing primitive useful for PCG exclusion, road-shoulder clearance and hit-mask padding, not a GPU shader, physics query, or persistent spatial index. A chunk-local mask has no knowledge of neighboring tiles unless the caller includes a border.

method.name: distance_transform_8
method.description: Cgame extension: produces a row-major 8-bit [i]chessboard/Chebyshev[/i] distance field from a binary [param mask]. Every nonzero mask pixel is a feature with distance 0, and all other pixels receive their minimum number of horizontal, vertical or diagonal grid steps to a feature. Uses two linear-time 8-neighbor raster passes; no Euclidean-distance or signed-distance approximation is implied. Diagonal steps cost one pixel just like cardinal steps, and feature positions outside the image are not considered. Values within [param max_distance] (inclusive) are returned as integers; 255 denotes no feature within the requested radius. A zero radius returns zeros for feature pixels and 255 elsewhere. [param size] must have both dimensions between 1 and 2048, the [param mask] must contain exactly [code]size.x * size.y[/code] bytes, and [param max_distance] must be between 0 and 254. Invalid input returns an empty array and reports an error. The input mask remains unchanged. This API operates on CPU data, not a GPU texture.

method.name: rasterize_segments_mask
method.description: Cgame extension: rasterizes a set of independent line segments into a row-major 8-bit grayscale mask. [param segment_endpoints] contains pairs [code][a0, b0, a1, b1, ...][/code] in pixel coordinates. The center of the first pixel is [code](0.5, 0.5)[/code]. Each segment is opaque (255) at distances less than or equal to [param half_width], fades linearly through the next [param softness] pixels, then becomes transparent (0). Overlapping segments combine by maximum coverage. A zero-length segment produces a round dab. Returns a [PackedByteArray] of length [code]size.x * size.y[/code] suitable for [constant Image.FORMAT_L8]. For safety, both dimensions must be between 1 and 2048, there may be at most 8192 segments, [param half_width] must be finite and nonnegative, [param softness] must be finite and positive, and all segment coordinates must be finite. Invalid input returns an empty array. Empty valid segment input returns a zeroed mask. Work is bounded to each segment's clipped pixel bounding box. No GPU work is performed.

method.name: get_closest_point_to_segment
method.description: Returns the 2D point on the 2D segment ([param s1], [param s2]) that is closest to [param point]. The returned point will always be inside the specified segment.

method.name: get_closest_point_to_segment_uncapped
method.description: Returns the 2D point on the 2D line defined by ([param s1], [param s2]) that is closest to [param point]. The returned point can be inside the segment ([param s1], [param s2]) or outside of it, i.e. somewhere on the line extending from the segment.

method.name: get_closest_points_between_segments
method.description: Given the two 2D segments ([param p1], [param q1]) and ([param p2], [param q2]), finds those two points on the two segments that are closest to each other. Returns a [PackedVector2Array] that contains this point on ([param p1], [param q1]) as well the accompanying point on ([param p2], [param q2]).

method.name: intersect_polygons
method.description: Intersects [param polygon_a] with [param polygon_b] and returns an array of intersected polygons. This performs [constant OPERATION_INTERSECTION] between polygons. In other words, returns common area shared by polygons. Returns an empty array if no intersection occurs. The operation may result in an outer polygon (boundary) and inner polygon (hole) produced which could be distinguished by calling [method is_polygon_clockwise].

method.name: intersect_polyline_with_polygon
method.description: Intersects [param polyline] with [param polygon] and returns an array of intersected polylines. This performs [constant OPERATION_INTERSECTION] between the polyline and the polygon. This operation can be thought of as chopping a line with a closed shape.

method.name: is_point_in_circle
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if [param point] is inside the circle or if it's located exactly [i]on[/i] the circle's boundary, otherwise returns [code]false[/code].

method.name: is_point_in_polygon
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if [param point] is inside [param polygon] or if it's located exactly [i]on[/i] polygon's boundary, otherwise returns [code]false[/code].

method.name: is_polygon_clockwise
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if [param polygon]'s vertices are ordered in clockwise order, otherwise returns [code]false[/code]. [b]Note:[/b] Assumes a Cartesian coordinate system where [code]+x[/code] is right and [code]+y[/code] is up. If using screen coordinates ([code]+y[/code] is down), the result will need to be flipped (i.e. a [code]true[/code] result will indicate counter-clockwise).

method.name: line_intersects_line
make_atlas
method.description: Given an array of [Vector2]s representing tiles, builds an atlas. The returned dictionary has two keys: [code]points[/code] is a [PackedVector2Array] that specifies the positions of each tile, [code]size[/code] contains the overall size of the whole atlas as [Vector2i].

method.name: merge_polygons
method.description: Merges (combines) [param polygon_a] and [param polygon_b] and returns an array of merged polygons. This performs [constant OPERATION_UNION] between polygons. The operation may result in an outer polygon (boundary) and multiple inner polygons (holes) produced which could be distinguished by calling [method is_polygon_clockwise].

method.name: offset_polygon
method.description: Inflates or deflates [param polygon] by [param delta] units (pixels). If [param delta] is positive, makes the polygon grow outward. If [param delta] is negative, shrinks the polygon inward. Returns an array of polygons because inflating/deflating may result in multiple discrete polygons. Returns an empty array if [param delta] is negative and the absolute value of it approximately exceeds the minimum bounding rectangle dimensions of the polygon. Each polygon's vertices will be rounded as determined by [param join_type]. The operation may result in an outer polygon (boundary) and inner polygon (hole) produced which could be distinguished by calling [method is_polygon_clockwise]. [b]Note:[/b] To translate the polygon's vertices specifically, multiply them to a [Transform2D]: [codeblocks] [gdscript] var polygon = PackedVector2Array([Vector2(0, 0), Vector2(100, 0), Vector2(100, 100), Vector2(0, 100)]) var offset = Vector2(50, 50) polygon = Transform2D(0, offset) * polygon print(polygon) # Prints [(50.0, 50.0), (150.0, 50.0), (150.0, 150.0), (50.0, 150.0)] [/gdscript] [csharp] Vector2[] polygon = [new Vector2(0, 0), new Vector2(100, 0), new Vector2(100, 100), new Vector2(0, 100)]; var offset = new Vector2(50, 50); polygon = new Transform2D(0, offset) * polygon; GD.Print((Variant)polygon); // Prints [(50, 50), (150, 50), (150, 150), (50, 150)] [/csharp] [/codeblocks]

method.name: offset_polyline
method.description: Inflates or deflates [param polyline] by [param delta] units (pixels), producing polygons. If [param delta] is positive, makes the polyline grow outward. Returns an array of polygons because inflating/deflating may result in multiple discrete polygons. If [param delta] is negative, returns an empty array. Each polygon's vertices will be rounded as determined by [param join_type]. Each polygon's endpoints will be rounded as determined by [param end_type]. The operation may result in an outer polygon (boundary) and inner polygon (hole) produced which could be distinguished by calling [method is_polygon_clockwise].

method.name: point_is_inside_triangle
method.description: Returns if [param point] is inside the triangle specified by [param a], [param b] and [param c].

method.name: segment_intersects_circle
method.description: Given the 2D segment ([param segment_from], [param segment_to]), returns the position on the segment (as a number between 0 and 1) at which the segment hits the circle that is located at position [param circle_position] and has radius [param circle_radius]. If the segment does not intersect the circle, -1 is returned (this is also the case if the line extending the segment would intersect the circle, but the segment does not).

method.name: segment_intersects_segment
method.description: Checks if two line segments intersect, with line [code]a[/code] between [param from_a] and [param to_a] and line [code]b[/code] between [param from_b] and [param to_b]. If the line segments intersect, the point of intersection is returned as a [Vector2]. If no intersection takes place, [code]null[/code] is returned.

method.name: triangulate_delaunay
method.description: Triangulates the area specified by discrete set of [param points] such that no point is inside the circumcircle of any resulting triangle. Returns a [PackedInt32Array] where each triangle consists of three consecutive point indices into [param points] (i.e. the returned array will have [code]n * 3[/code] elements, with [code]n[/code] being the number of found triangles). If the triangulation did not succeed, an empty [PackedInt32Array] is returned.

method.name: triangulate_polygon
method.description: Triangulates the polygon specified by the points in [param polygon]. Returns a [PackedInt32Array] where each triangle consists of three consecutive point indices into [param polygon] (i.e. the returned array will have [code]n * 3[/code] elements, with [code]n[/code] being the number of found triangles). Output triangles will always be counter clockwise, and the contour will be flipped if it's clockwise. If the triangulation did not succeed, an empty [PackedInt32Array] is returned.

constants.constant: Create regions where either subject or clip polygons (or both) are filled.
Create regions where subject polygons are filled except where clip polygons are filled.
Create regions where both subject and clip polygons are filled.
Create regions where either subject or clip polygons are filled but not where both are filled.
Squaring is applied uniformally at all convex edge joins at [code]1 * delta[/code].
While flattened paths can never perfectly trace an arc, they are approximated by a series of arc chords.

There's a necessary limit to mitered joins since offsetting edges that join at very acute angles will produce excessively long and narrow "spikes". For any given edge join, when miter offsetting would exceed that maximum distance, "square" joining is applied.
Endpoints are joined using the [enum PolyJoinType] value and the path filled as a polygon.
Endpoints are joined using the [enum PolyJoinType] value and the path filled as a polyline.
Endpoints are squared off with no extension.
Endpoints are squared off and extended by [code]delta[/code] units.
Endpoints are rounded off and extended by [code]delta[/code] units.
